subject: Zero-persistence evidence & mitigation plan

Subject: Zero-persistence evidence & mitigation plan

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same plan: 

- Goal: validate that Redwood can run an initial pilot with effectively zero persistence of model inputs/outputs for MedAI POC.
- What you asked for: concrete evidence of no-write guarantees, a technical design doc we can share with your security team, and a recommended mitigation plan for the pilot (scope, telemetry minimization, controls).

What we’re delivering in this thread: attached design doc and a short mitigation checklist; Aditya (privacy/infra) will respond with the technical controls and SOC2 snapshot.

Action items I’ll take:
- Share the design doc (attached) describing memory-only inference flow and options to disable any persistent logging on the pilot cluster.
- Schedule a 30–45 min security walkthrough with your team (suggest Tue or Thu next week).

Could you confirm the scope for the pilot (number of sessions / traffic profile) and whether MedAI requires VPC-only connectivity or on-prem options? If you want, we can include a temporary ACL that restricts egress while the pilot runs.

Attachments: redwood_zero_persistence_design.pdf (design), pilot_mitigation_checklist.xlsx (steps & verification)

Thanks — I’ll let Aditya follow up with the technical specifics.

Best,

Subject: Re: Zero-persistence evidence & mitigation plan

Thanks, Irene — good call. A few clarifying questions from our security team before we set the walkthrough: 

1) "Zero persistence" is a strong ask. We need explicit details on where model inputs/outputs may touch disk across the stack (inference node swap, kernel OOMs, OS-level pagefiles). Can you confirm whether any write-to-disk is possible in default and in proposed pilot config?
2) How do you handle logs: request logs, access logs, and debug dumps? For the pilot we want those disabled (or only hashed telemetry retained). Is that feasible?
3) Third-party integrations: if we use S3-backed artifacts or monitoring agents, what guarantees exist that those agents won't snapshot raw inputs?
4) Data residency: pilot must run in us-west-2; do you support a dedicated VPC and customer-managed KMS for the pilot?

We have a security questionnaire attached with low, medium, high risk items — happy to send the completed copy back after your answers: medai_security_qs.xlsx

If you can provide the design doc and a short one-page attestation (or SOC2 excerpt) that covers data-at-rest/no-storage controls, that will help speed approval. Also please include a proposed date for the walkthrough.

—Alice
Alice Bennett
Director, Product Security | MedAI Health
alice.bennett@medaihealth.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@medaihealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 06 Aug 2026 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zero-persistence evidence & mitigation plan

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise technical response and the pilot controls we propose. I’ve attached the detailed design and a short SOC2 snapshot that references our logging and storage controls.

High-level answers: 
- Disk persistence: By default, Redwood’s hosted runtime uses an in-memory KV cache (RAM) for model context. For the pilot we will:
  * Run inference with KV caching disabled (stateless mode) to ensure no context kept between requests.
  * Disable on-node local persistence: we will pass runtime flags to prevent any temp file writes (we also disable OS-level core dumps for the pilot).
  * Use an ephemeral filesystem mount (tmpfs) where any OS-level writes are memory-backed and not persisted to local disk.

- Logs and telemetry:
  * Request/response bodies are not logged by default in the pilot. We will disable request logging and keep only hashed, redacted metrics (e.g., latency percentiles, error counters) for 90 days at aggregate level unless you request shorter retention.
  * Access logs will contain only request IDs and non-identifying metadata (no payloads).
  * Debug dumps are disabled; debug-mode toggles require engineering approval and cannot be enabled in the pilot without explicit sign-off from MedAI security.

- Third-party agents:
  * No sidecars that persist raw inputs will be installed. Monitoring will be via a metrics exporter that sends aggregated stats only. Any S3 usage is configurable and will be disabled for the pilot; if artifact storage is required, we will use an encrypted bucket in your VPC and provide a separate agreement for access.

- Residency & KMS:
  * We support us-west-2 region for Dedicated or Private deployments. For the pilot we can provision a dedicated VPC peering and support customer-managed KMS keys (bring-your-own-key) for any artifacts that must be encrypted.

Proposed pilot controls (summary):
1) Stateless inference mode (no KV caching).
2) tmpfs for any temporary files; core dumps disabled.
3) No request/response logging; only hashed metrics retained.
4) Dedicated VPC with egress ACLs; optional BYOK for KMS.
5) SOC2 snapshot and design doc attached for review.

Attachments: redwood_zero_persistence_design.pdf, pilot_mitigation_checklist.xlsx, redwood_soc2-snapshot.txt

Next steps:
- We can do a 45-min walkthrough on Mon Aug 10 or Tue Aug 11. Which works best for your security team?
- If accepted, we’ll stand up the pilot cluster and provide ephemeral credentials and a short test plan (20–50 sessions) so you can validate no persistence.

If you want, we can also include a short cryptographic attestation describing key handling and rotation during the pilot.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer, Privacy Controls | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 06 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zero-persistence evidence & mitigation plan

Thanks Aditya — that level of detail helps a lot. We are prepared to run a limited pilot under those controls. Confirmed items:
- Pilot scope: 25 concurrent sessions, capped to 1000 total requests over 72 hours.
- Region: us-west-2, dedicated VPC, BYOK KMS.
- Logging: request bodies must not be stored; access logs limited to request ID + time.

We’ll schedule the walkthrough with our security team on Mon Aug 10 at 11:00 PT. Please send a calendar invite and a short test plan that includes the exact API calls we will run and the verification steps MedAI will perform.

Also please send the SOC2 excerpt and the cryptographic attestation you mentioned. If everything checks out after the pilot, we’ll move forward with a short-term purchase order.

—Alice
Alice Bennett
Director, Product Security | MedAI Health
